title: Part 1
text: Meet the strangest traveler in the pond. It is a flatworm, it has no brain, and it needs three different kinds of animals to finish its life.

title: Part 2
text: Think about how strange that is.
nxt: A single brainless worm needs a snail, an amphibian, and a bird, all in the right place at the right time, just to finish one lap of its life.

title: Part 3
text: Step one is the ramshorn snail. A microscopic swimming larva called a miracidium burrows into the snail's soft tissue.

title: Part 4
text: Step two begins after some weeks, when the clones mature into a free-swimming stage called cercariae.
nxt: A single infected snail can release large numbers of these fork-tailed swimmers into the water. They have no mouths, and their energy reserves are limited.

title: Part 5
text: That host is a developing tadpole. At this delicate stage, small clusters of cells called limb buds are forming near the base of its tail.
nxt: They hold the instructions for growing two matched hind legs. And the cercariae head straight for that spot.

title: Part 6
text: On contact, the parasite attacks the skin. It sheds its swimming tail, pushes its small body through the tissue, and burrows toward the limb bud.

title: Part 7
text: Once settled deep inside the limb-forming area, it builds a thick wall around itself. It becomes an immobile, armored cyst called a metacercaria.
